**Coaching Note (for club player at 1500 level):**

Your king walked into danger on c6. After Black played g6, look for checks that force your opponent's king to a worse square. Here, R1b6+ forces Kd5—the only legal move. Then Rxd6+ is a classic rook fork: it checks the king AND attacks the d6 pawn. Your opponent loses material and the game. When you see two rooks attacking along the same file, think about checks that gain tempo and win material.
